Core explanation · 00:00–04:59

In this session, we will discuss formation of partial differential equation by elimination of arbitrary functions, solutions of partial differential equations, and solution of first order equations.

Key details

  • Remember, there are two ways to form a PDE.
  • That is by elimination of arbitrary constants and by elimination of arbitrary functions.
  • In a similar manner, a second order equation may arise from an expression containing.
  • Two arbitrary functions.
  • Remember, it is not always guaranteed that an nth order PDE can be formed from an equation involving n arbitrary functions.
  • In some cases, higher order.
  • Partial derivatives may be required to eliminate all n arbitrary functions.
  • That leads to a PDE of harder higher than n.
  • In these cases, the obtain PDE may not be unique.
  • For a partial differential equation from an arbitrary function z equals f of x plus y.
  • Observe that in this question we have f to be an arbitrary function.
  • Because there is only one arbitrary function.
  • We proceed by finding first order partial derivatives.
  • That's going to be f dash of u times dou by dou x.
  • Since u equals x plus y, dou u by dou x becomes 1.
  • Because U is a function of X and T.
  • So w by dou x becomes f dash of x plus ct plus g dash of x minus c t and w by dou t equals f dash of x plus c t times c plus g dash of x minus ct times minus c because the coefficient of minus c t with respect to t is minus c.
  • Since there are two arbitrary functions, we need second derivative also.
  • We get f dash of x plus ct plus g double dash of x minus ct.

Core explanation · 10:00–14:59

Let's look at what is a complete solution and what is general solution.

Key details

  • A solution of a PDE is said to be complete solution if the number of arbitrary consents is same as the number of independent variables present in a PDE.
  • Let Z equals f of x plus y.
  • We need to form a PDE by eliminating this arbitrary function f.
  • It is very easy to see that we can eliminate f dash of x space y by equating dou z by doux and dou z by dou y.
  • The equation dou z by dou x minus dou z by dou y equals zero is a partial differential equation formed by eliminating arbitrary function from the original function.
  • So an equation containing XYZPQ defines a first order PDE which we have seen already in the session number one.
  • A relation of the form phi of UV equals zero where phi is an arbitrary function of u and v.
  • and satisfies equation one is called a general solution.
  • In a similar manner, the solution obtained by determining the arbitrary function in the general solution by using some specified condition is called a particular solution.
  • We will look at the idea of general solution once again in Lagrange's linear equation.
  • We understood the idea of solution of PDEs.
  • We also learned solution of first order equations.
